laws.rule: Machu Picchu tickets are sold only directly to the visitor or registered agencies through the Ministry of Culture's TuBoleto platform or authorised DDC Cusco offices. Tickets are nominal, tied to date, time, circuit and the holder's passport; no name or date changes.
laws.heading: RM 334-2026-MC, art. 15

laws.rule: Enter with your ticket and original passport (foreign visitors); staff may ask for both inside the site. A guide is recommended, not compulsory.
laws.heading: RM 334-2026-MC, art. 17

laws.rule: An unused ticket is void after its date and time; no rescheduling or refunds except proven force majeure.
laws.heading: RM 334-2026-MC, art. 15.5

laws.rule: Boleto Turístico del Cusco (Cusco tourist ticket), sold by COSITUC, prices for foreign visitors: integral ticket S/130, valid 10 days, for circuits I to III; partial tickets for one circuit S/70; student ticket S/70 (ages 10 to 17 with ID; 18 to 25 with a current student or ISIC card). Circuit I: Saqsaywaman, Q'enqo, Puka Pukara, Tambomachay. Circuit II: Qorikancha site museum, Regional History Museum, Museum of Contemporary Art, Pachacuteq Monument, Museum of Popular Art, Centro Qosqo de Arte Nativo, Tipón, Pikillaqta. Circuit III: Ollantaytambo, Pisaq, Chinchero, Moray. (No RBA rate for PEN; A$1 = about 2.4408 PEN (Banco Central de Reserva del Perú, 30 October 2026, crossed via the RBA USD rate of 30 October 2026): S/130 ≈ A$53.26; S/70 ≈ A$28.68)

Boleto Turístico del Cusco added 5 November 2026; its page lists partial II and III as valid 2 days, which reads inconsistently, so validity of partial tickets is not recorded.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: At Machu Picchu it is prohibited to bring bags over 40x35x20 cm, food, alcohol, illegal substances, aerosols, umbrellas, tripods, selfie sticks or stabilisers, prams, hard-soled shoes or heels; to make loud noise (clapping, shouting, whistling, singing); to jump, lie down, run or undress; to smoke, vape or light fires; or to drop rubbish.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: Don't climb on or lean against walls, or touch, move or remove stones. Activities that undermine the sacred character of the Llaqta (fashion shoots, dances, social engagements, obscene acts) are banned, as are advertising banners, costumes and commercial filming.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: Ministerio de Cultura del Perú (Dirección Desconcentrada de Cultura Cusco), Machupicchu site administration.

festivals.what: Inti Raymi (festival of the Sun) on 24 June, staged by EMUFEC, the Cusco municipal festivals company, with performances at Qorikancha, the Plaza Mayor and Saqsaywaman. EMUFEC publishes the ticket prices for the Saqsaywaman stands each year; the 2027 programme isn't out yet.
